newsitem.title: FINLAND: FINNISH TT TIETO SEES BOOST FROM EURO.
newsitem.headline: FINNISH TT TIETO SEES BOOST FROM EURO.

text.p: Finnish information technology group TT Tieto Oy said on Friday it expected rapid growth in the next few years from data system changes required by the launch of a single European currency, and increased electronic trading.
The turn of the millenium, introducing a new first digit to dates, would also boost demand, the company said.
"The next two to three years will be a period of strong growth in demand for data services," TT Tieto CEO Matti Lehti told a news conference.
Lehti said the value of data system changes connected to the launch in Finland of Europe's single currency would be several billions of markka in the next few years.

TT Tieto's net sales could roughly double in the next three to four years purely on the demand created by the switch to the euro, he said, adding the outcome would depend on how well the company rose to the challenge.
A projected increase in electronic trading would also boost demand for information technology services, he said.
"Early in the next millennium, electronic trading will already be significant," Lehti said.

In 1996, TT Tieto's net sales rose to 2.05 billion markka from 1.15 billion. In the results report, TT Tieto said 1997 net sales growth would be closer to its 15 percent annual growth target after an "exceptional merger year" 1996.
The average annual organic growth rate of the data services market was five to 10 percent, Lehti said.
TT Tieto's profit before extraordinary items doubled in 1996 to 194 million markka.
